additions.reason: The good point found within oneself; explicitly stated as a bechina of חָסִיד. Belongs to the domain of holiness — finding merit and goodness.
additions.source_quote: וְלִמְצֹא בְּעַצְמוֹ אֵיזֶה זְכוּת וּנְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה, אֲשֶׁר בִּבְחִינַת הַנְּקֻדָּה טוֹבָה הַזֹּאת הוּא בְּחִינַת חָסִיד

additions.reason: The pious one; explicitly equated via bechina to the nekuda tova (good point). When a person finds their good point, in that aspect they are a chasid.
additions.source_quote: אֲשֶׁר בִּבְחִינַת הַנְּקֻדָּה טוֹבָה הַזֹּאת הוּא בְּחִינַת חָסִיד

analysis_notes.summary: Torah #125 discusses saying Tehillim and applying every psalm to oneself. The source text contains one explicit bechina relationship: נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה is בְּחִינַת חָסִיד. Neither concept appears in the dataset for this torah (ref 1125 has 0 edges). The remaining concepts (Tehillim, David HaMelekh, milchemet ha-yetzer, kaf zchut, Yehoshafat) are connected by eitza/practical-advice logic rather than bechina. This torah cross-references LM1 Torah #282 (Azamra) which is the major teaching on finding good points.
